2855-elissa-or-the-doom-of-zimbabwe.title: Elissa Or The Doom Of Zimbabwe
2855-elissa-or-the-doom-of-zimbabwe.creator: H. Rider Haggard
2855-elissa-or-the-doom-of-zimbabwe.description: A book by H. Rider Haggard. The world is full of ruins, but few of them have an origin so utterly lost in mystery as those of Zimbabwe in South Central Africa. What purpose did they serve? These are questions that must have perplexed many generations, and many different races of men.

56986-the-babe-b-a-being-the-uneventful-.title: The Babe B A Being The Uneventful History Of A Young Gentlem
56986-the-babe-b-a-being-the-uneventful-.creator: Unknown
56986-the-babe-b-a-being-the-uneventful-.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. _So that, now it is complete, you will find therein neither births, deaths, nor marriages, and though the =Babe= himself may have waxed a little out of proportion to our original scheme--he ought, for instance, never to have played Rugby for his University, as savouring too much of the hero--I have retained for him to the end that futility of mind, and girt him about with that flippant atmosphere, in which the truly heroic chokes and stifles.

arxiv-2201-08339.title: Σ \Sigma -semicommutative rings and their skew PBW extensions Thanks: The authors were supported by the research fund of Faculty of Science, Code HERMES 52464, Universidad Nacional de Colombia - Sede Bogotá, Colombia.
arxiv-2201-08339.creator: Héctor Suárez, Armando Reyes
arxiv-2201-08339.description: Abstract . In this paper, we introduce the concept of Σ \Sigma -semicommutative ring, for Σ \Sigma a finite family of endomorphisms of a ring R R . We relate this class of rings with other classes of rings such that Abelian, reduced, Σ \Sigma -rigid, nil-reversible and rings satisfying the Σ \Sigma -skew reflexive nilpotent property.

arxiv-2205-13410.title: Equation-free surrogate modeling of geophysical flows at the intersection of machine learning and data assimilation
arxiv-2205-13410.creator: Suraj Pawar, Omer San
arxiv-2205-13410.description: Abstract There is a growing interest in developing data-driven reduced-order models for atmospheric and oceanic flows that are trained on data obtained either from high-resolution simulations or satellite observations. The data-driven models are non-intrusive in nature and offer significant computational savings compared to large-scale numerical models.

arxiv-2409-02371.title: Unfolding Videos Dynamics via Taylor Expansion
arxiv-2409-02371.creator: Siyi Chen, Minkyu Choi, Zesen Zhao, Kuan Han, Qing Qu, Zhongming Liu
arxiv-2409-02371.description: Abstract Taking inspiration from physical motion, we present a new self-supervised dynamics learning strategy for videos: Vi deo Time- Di fferentiation for Instance Di scrimination (ViDiDi). ViDiDi is a simple and data-efficient strategy, readily applicable to existing self-supervised video representation learning frameworks based on instance discrimination.

arxiv-2501-06811.title: Signals for a 2HDM with Z ′ Z^{\prime} at the LHC
arxiv-2501-06811.creator: Anjan Kumar Barik, Santosh Kumar Rai, Agnivo Sarkar
arxiv-2501-06811.description: Abstract We consider a neutrinophilic U ⁡ ( 1 ) U(1) extension of the Standard Model (SM) under which only a second Higgs doublet and SM singlet scalars and fermions are charged. The new gauge boson Z ′ Z^{\prime} couples to SM minimally, generated by Z − Z ′ Z-Z^{\prime} mixing.

arxiv-2508-02124.title: Trainable Dynamic Mask Sparse Attention
arxiv-2508-02124.creator: Jingze Shi, Yifan Wu, Bingheng Wu, Yiran Peng, Liangdong Wang, Guang Liu, Yuyu Luo
arxiv-2508-02124.description: Abstract In large language models, the demand for modeling long contexts is constantly increasing, but the quadratic complexity of the standard self-attention mechanism often becomes a bottleneck. Although existing sparse attention mechanisms have improved efficiency, they may still encounter issues such as static patterns or information loss.

arxiv-2510-16751.title: Visual Autoregressive Models Beat Diffusion Models on Inference Time Scaling
arxiv-2510-16751.creator: Erik Riise, Mehmet Onurcan Kaya, Dim P. Papadopoulos
arxiv-2510-16751.description: Abstract While inference-time scaling through search has revolutionized Large Language Models, translating these gains to image generation has proven difficult. Recent attempts to apply search strategies to continuous diffusion models show limited benefits, with simple random sampling often performing best. We demonstrate that the discrete, sequential nature of visual autoregressive models enables effective search for image generation.

arxiv-2602-07399.title: VGAS: Value-Guided Action-Chunk Selection for Few-Shot Vision-Language-Action Adaptation
arxiv-2602-07399.creator: Changhua Xu, Jie Lu, Junyu Xuan, En Yu
arxiv-2602-07399.description: Abstract Vision–Language–Action (VLA) models bridge multimodal reasoning with physical control, but adapting them to new tasks with scarce demonstrations remains unreliable. While fine-tuned VLA policies often produce semantically plausible trajectories, failures often arise from unresolved geometric ambiguities, where near-miss action candidates lead to divergent execution outcomes under limited supervision.

pmc-11433087.title: Treatment of Severe Asthma: Case Report of Fast Action of Mepolizumab in a Patient with Recent SARS-CoV-2 Infection
pmc-11433087.creator: Cristiana Indolfi, Giulio Dinardo, Angela Klain, Fabio Decimo, Michele Miraglia del Giudice, Antonio Caputi, Jarosław Walory
pmc-11433087.description: Asthma is one of the most common chronic inflammatory diseases of childhood with a heterogeneous impact on health and quality of life. Mepolizumab is an antagonist of interleukin-5, indicated as an adjunct therapy for severe refractory eosinophilic asthma in adolescents and children aged >6 years old.

pmc-11506062.title: Insights into Metabolic Reprogramming in Tumor Evolution and Therapy
pmc-11506062.creator: Ching-Feng Chiu, Jonathan Jaime G. Guerrero, Ric Ryan H. Regalado, Jiayan Zhou, Kin Israel Notarte, Yu-Wei Lu, Paolo C. Encarnacion, Cidne Danielle D. Carles, Edrian M. Octavo, Dan Christopher I. Limbaroc, Charupong Saengboonmee, Shih-Yi Huang
pmc-11506062.description: Simple SummaryCancer is a global health problem caused by uncontrolled cell growth and changes in how cells get and use energy. This review compares cancer’s hidden metabolic changes to dark matter and dark energy in the universe, which are mysterious and often ignored.

pmc-12747239.title: Optic disc edema associated with neuroborreliosis
pmc-12747239.creator: Molly Barten, Eliisa Strand, Tyler Knight
pmc-12747239.description: PurposeOptic disc edema as the primary ocular manifestation of Lyme disease is rare. Current knowledge of the presentation and treatment of optic disc edema in neuroborreliosis relies on case reports. This case presents successful treatment of neuroborreliosis associated optic disc edema in a pediatric patient.

pmc-12827180.title: The nutritional environment and food access of female athletes at HBCUs: a qualitative analysis
pmc-12827180.creator: Nancy A. Uriegas, Zachary K. Winkelmann, Dawn M. Emerson, Toni M. Torres-McGehee
pmc-12827180.description: PurposeFemale student-athletes attending Historically Black Colleges and Universities (HBCUs) may encounter distinct challenges related to food access, particularly when their campuses are situated in areas with limited food availability. This study assessed food security (FS) and explored the lived experiences of HBCU female student-athletes regarding their food environments and access to nutrition.

pmc-13087886.title: The Cyclic Adenosine Monophosphate Phosphodiesterase CpdA Modulates cAMP Homeostasis, Stress Adaptability, Biofilm Formation, Motility, Quorum Sensing and Antibiotic Resistance of Aeromonas veronii
pmc-13087886.creator: Wenjing Yang, Xiaolei Wang, Shengyuan Zhou, Guina Yu, Xiaoyan Zhou, Zhihai Sui
pmc-13087886.description: Aeromonas veronii, a Gram-negative pathogen, is ubiquitous in nature and infects broad hosts, which becomes a serious threat to the public health. The cyclic adenosine monophosphate (cAMP), precisely modulated by cyclic nucleotide phosphodiesterase (PDE), regulates key cellular processes in bacteria. However, the specific function and regulatory role of PDE in A. veronii remain unclear.

pmc-13248531.title: Safety evaluation of an extension of use of the food enzyme glucan 1,4‐α‐maltohydrolase from the genetically modified Bacillus licheniformis strain NZYM‐CY
pmc-13248531.creator: EFSA Panel on Food Enzymes (FEZ), Holger Zorn, José Manuel Barat Baviera, Claudia Bolognesi, Francesco Catania, Gabriele Gadermaier, Ralf Greiner, Baltasar Mayo, Alicja Mortensen, Yrjö Henrik Roos, Marize L M Solano, Henk Van Loveren, Laurence Vernis, Irene Bonino, Daniele Cavanna, Yi Liu
pmc-13248531.description: The food enzyme glucan 1,4‐α‐maltohydrolase (4‐α‐d‐glucan α‐maltohydrolase, EC 3.2.1.133) is produced with the genetically modified Bacillus licheniformis strain NZYM‐CY by Novozymes A/S. The safety of this food enzyme was evaluated previously and it did not give rise to safety concerns when used in three food manufacturing processes.

pmc-13271867.title: Burn Wound Infections With Staphylococcus aureus : Clinical Characteristics and Risk Factors for Methicillin‐Resistant Strains
pmc-13271867.creator: Xiaolan Hong, Shaobo Zhou, Qinghua Cai, Yuanyuan Cai, Zhaohong Chen, Wanting Zhao, Yongjian Ye, Xubo Dai
pmc-13271867.description: This study aimed to systematically delineate the clinical characteristics and identify the key risk factors associated with methicillin‐resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) infections in burn patients, thereby informing targeted preventive measures and therapeutic strategies. This retrospective study included 270 burn patients with Staphylococcus aureus (S. aureus ) infections at a Chinese centre (2019–2022), comprising 127 MRSA and 143 methicillin‐susceptible S.

pmc-13272736.title: Research progress and prospects of nanomaterials in imaging of central nervous system diseases
pmc-13272736.creator: Houfan Li, Lihua Deng, Zongqian Wu, Chen Liu
pmc-13272736.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Nanomaterials have garnered significant attention in recent years for their application in the imaging of central nervous system diseases (CNSDs). To comprehensively understand the research progress and trends in this field, this paper conducted a bibliometric analysis of relevant literature over the past fourteen years, systematically reviewing the research hotspots and development trends in the application of nanomaterials for CNSDs imaging.

pmc-13627428.title: Lactiplantibacillus plantarum peptides and probiotics from peanut butter enhance antimicrobial activity and gut microbiota modulation
pmc-13627428.creator: Mansour Alblaji, Shaaban H. Moussa
pmc-13627428.description: BackgroundFermented plant matrices with probiotics show antimicrobial and gut health potential. Still, the quantitative links between peanut fermentation, peptide–probiotic synergy, digestive survival, and microbiota modulation remain unclear.ObjectiveWe optimized bioactive peptide production from reduced-fat (33%) and full-fat (50%) peanut butter fermented with Lactiplantibacillus plantarum ATCC 14917 for 0–72 h using a full factorial design.
